title: The Lost Story Page
markdown:
Luna the little lamb and Milo the meadow mouse were snuggled warm in their bed. Moonbeams came through the window like soft silver ribbons. They made quiet shapes on the rug. The room was hushed. Milo’s whiskers wobbled. His eyes were already half closed. He gave a little sleepy yawn.

Luna’s wool felt like warm cotton. “Time for our story, Milo?” she whispered.

Milo nodded. His nose wiggled. He tucked deeper into his mossy pillow.

Luna reached for their favourite book. The cover was worn smooth from many nights. It had pictures of fluffy clouds and sleepy sheep. She opened it to the very last page — the page where the sheep find their softest meadow.

The last page was gone.

Luna’s brow made a small ripple. “Where did the last page go?”

Milo blinked, calm as always. His eyes were dark like little polished pebbles. “Let’s look gently,” he murmured.

So they looked. They moved as quiet as falling snow.

First they looked under the warm blankets. Only cozy fluff. Only sleepy dust that sparkled a little in the dim.

Then Luna peeked behind Maelor the Bear, their big cuddly friend who smelled of sunshine and warm honey. Maelor’s button eyes looked back. His plush arms rested. He did not have the page. He only sat, soft and still, the way he always sat.

Milo tiptoed to the toy basket. Soft balls. Gentle rattles. He nudged a little blue woolly ball. It rolled. More quiet shadows. No page.

They looked and looked. Soft whispers. Soft steps. The room stayed peaceful. Their breathing stayed slow. The last page was still not there.

Then Luna noticed the window sill.

Moonlight lay on it in a small bright patch. And resting on the sill, like a fallen feather, was a piece of paper. Thin. Delicate. It looked just like the last page.

Milo scampered over on quiet paws. Luna followed. Her lamb steps were barely a whisper on the rug.

There it was. The very last page. The moon had found it first.

They picked it up with care. Luna held it against her warm wool. Milo nestled close. They read the last few words together — words about sweet dreams, and cozy naps, and the moon watching with a sleepy eye. The words felt like a slow warm river. A meadow. Grass as soft as a sigh.

When they finished the very last word, a sleepy feeling spread through them, warm as a blanket. Their eyes grew heavy. They snuggled back into bed, the page safe in the book again, hearts beating a slow happy rhythm.

The moon kept watch. The ribbons on the rug grew still. Luna and Milo were ready for the sweetest slumber.
characters: Luna (a little lamb), Milo (a meadow mouse)
